text: Despite the paucity of objective evidence, a logical case can be made that TUT does play a role in hypertrophy. However, it appears the effects are more related to the time a muscle is worked over the duration of a training session than to the TUT for a given set. In support of this hypothesis, my lab showed that performing a powerlifting-style workout consisting of 7 sets of 3RM produced increases in muscle growth similar to those of a bodybuilding-style workout consisting of 3 sets of 10RM (208). Although TUT in the powerlifting-style sets was markedly lower than in the bodybuilding-style sets (~9 seconds vs. ~30 seconds, respectively), the total TUT for the training session was approximately equal because of the greater number of sets performed for the powerlifting-style condition.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 4: Role of Resistance Training Variables in Hypertrophy
